how-much-to-charge-to-replace-a-boiler.h.text:
← Boiler replacement bid calculator

How much to charge to replace a boiler

Hydronic and steam techs get shopped on a published $4,500 installed boiler Facebook special. Those numbers cannot see the system or the extras. An 80 MBH gas hot-water like-for-like swap with two zones is a different job from a 140 MBH oil steam-to-hot-water conversion with four zones, an indirect tank, and a chimney liner.

Open the free boiler replacement bid calculator

Price the plant and the extras, not the $4,500 dump

A boiler changeout is a plant, then a system, then how much of that plant is actually sold. Like-for-like drops a same-fuel, same-system boiler in the same size class. A condensing upgrade is a vent and condensate change. Steam-to-hot-water is a piping job plus the plant. Hot water is circulators and zone valves. Steam is a Hartford loop and a low-water cutoff.

Like-for-like is not a steam conversion

The cheap special is almost always an 80 MBH gas hydronic swap, two zones, no liner, no indirect. A steam-to-hot-water conversion is a different crew week. Matching a per-MBH number on a conversion job is how a sold boiler becomes a loss when the piping and the liner eat the margin.

This is not a furnace, a water heater, or a mini-split

A furnace is forced air, AFUE, and a matching coil. A water heater is a tank or tankless, not a hydronic plant. A mini-split is a line-set and heads. A fireplace insert is a liner in a firebox. A chimney sweep is a flue cleaning. This prices a boiler changeout: input MBH, system, scope, and extras.

Walk-away price

Load the wage with payroll burden. Add overhead as a share of direct cost. Then take margin as a share of the customer’s price, not a markup on cost. The walk-away number is total cost. A proposed price under that number loses money before you take anything out of it.

This page is a walkthrough of the arithmetic in the boiler replacement bid calculator. Standing on a no-heat call? Should I patch this boiler for one more winter? They already bought the unit? Should I install a customer-supplied boiler? Saturday no-heat? Should I take a Saturday boiler call? It is not a heat-loss calculation, a fuel-gas code determination, a chimney design, or a price you should copy onto a contract.

Common questions

How much should I charge to replace a boiler?

Charge from input MBH, system, scope, and extras — not a published $4,500 boiler special. An 80 MBH gas hot-water like-for-like swap with two zones is a different job from a 140 MBH oil steam-to-hot-water conversion with four zones, an indirect tank, and a chimney liner.

Is a like-for-like swap the same bid as a steam-to-hot-water conversion?

No. Like-for-like drops a same-fuel, same-system plant in the same size class. A condensing upgrade is a vent and condensate change. Steam-to-hot-water is a piping job plus the plant. Matching a boiler special on a steam conversion is how a sold changeout becomes a loss when the piping and the liner eat the margin.

How do zones, a liner, and an indirect change a boiler price?

Hot water is circulators and zone valves. Steam is a Hartford loop and a low-water cutoff. An indirect water heater, a chimney liner, oil-to-gas, and primary/secondary piping do not live in a published boiler special.

Is this the same as a furnace, a water heater, or a mini-split?

No. A furnace is forced air, AFUE, and a matching coil. A water heater is a tank or tankless, not a hydronic plant. A mini-split is a line-set and heads. This prices a boiler changeout: input MBH, system, scope, and extras.

should-i-install-a-customer-supplied-boi.text:
← Boiler replacement bid calculator

Should I install a customer-supplied boiler?

Owners call with a crate in the driveway: “I already bought the boiler at Ferguson. Can you just hang it for $4,500?” That sounds like free margin because the plant invoice left the bid. It did not leave the trip, the near-boiler piping, the hang hours, or the chance that the crate is a steam boiler on a hydronic house.

Open the free boiler replacement bid calculator

Zeroing the plant is not a free changeout

A tech-supplied 80 MBH gas like-for-like still carries the boiler invoice. An owner-supplied unit that actually matches zeros that line and keeps the same hang hours. On a typical two-zone gas hot-water house — $48 wage, 32% burden, 15% overhead, 20% target margin, ten miles — the tech-supplied bid is about $6,741 (walk-away $5,393). Zeroing a $2,400 plant plus the fuel add-on drops it to about $2,428 (walk-away $1,943). Taking the Facebook hang-only number while you still buy the boiler loses about $893. The same $4,500 covers the set if their unit actually matches.

You supplyThey supply, it matchesThey supply, wrong unit
Plant invoice in the bidYesNoNo
Hang hoursSameSameSame, plus a callback
Bid on the sample rates$6,741$2,428$3,277
At $4,500 hang-onlyLoses $893Covers the setCovers, after a second trip

Wrong unit is a second trip

Supply-house shelves and online crates default to whatever was on sale. Plenty of houses are steam, sealed-combustion, or a different MBH. Setting the wrong plant means adapters, a dry-fit, or a drive back to exchange it. Price that callback on the same plant before you agree. The calculator adds a starting second trip, extra near-boiler hours, and an adapter kit on top of the rates you already typed. On the sample house that puts about $849 back on the owner-supplied bid.

How to use the comparison

Open the boiler replacement bid calculator, enter the plant you are standing in, and put their hang-only number in “price you’re considering.” The who-supplies table scores that number against you-supply, owner-supplies-it-matches, and owner-supplies-wrong-unit. Nothing is uploaded.

This is the same arithmetic as how much to charge to replace a boiler. It is not a heat-loss calculation, a fuel-gas code determination, a chimney design, or a reason to refuse a customer — it is the walk-away number on each supply path. A furnace is forced air. A water heater is a tank. This prices a hydronic or steam plant.

Common questions

Should I install a boiler the customer bought at a supply house?

Only after you price the hang without the plant invoice. Setting their crate is still a trip, near-boiler piping, and crew hours. A $4,500 hang-only special often sits under the walk-away on a tech-supplied job even when the same number covers the hang if their unit actually matches.

Does a customer-supplied boiler make the $4,500 installed special profitable?

It can, if the unit matches. Zeroing a $2,400 gas like-for-like invoice drops the bid, but loaded labor, travel, zones, and overhead stay. On a typical 80 MBH two-zone gas hot-water house the tech-supplied walk-away is still above $4,500. The owner-supplied walk-away sits under that number when the crate is the right system and size.

What if the supply-house boiler is the wrong system or size?

That is a second dispatch plus adapters or an exchange. A steam crate on a hydronic house, an atmospheric on a sealed-combustion vent, or the wrong MBH is not a free hang. Price that callback on the same plant before you agree to set whatever they rolled into the driveway.

should-i-patch-this-boiler-for-one-more-.text:
← Boiler replacement bid calculator

Should I patch this boiler for one more winter?

Owners call at 9 p.m.: “Can you just replace the circulator for $280 and get us through the winter?” That sounds cheaper than a plant bid because the boiler invoice left the ticket. It did not leave the trip, the loaded wage, or the two more no-heat calls a leaking heat exchanger actually produces before April.

Open the free boiler replacement bid calculator

The $280 special is a visit, not a season

A circulator swap still carries travel, on-site hours, and parts. On a typical 80 MBH gas hot-water house — $48 wage, 32% burden, 15% overhead, 20% target margin, ten miles — the visit walk-away sits above $280. Taking the Facebook number to “just get them heat tonight” still loses money even when three winters of honest patches still undercut a like-for-like replacement.

A cracked section is a different winter

A leaking heat exchanger or a cracked section does not stay fixed after one gasket. Price the extra calls this winter and the winters they want the old plant. When those callbacks carry real parts, the season can pass the replacement bid while the $280 visit is still a loss. That is the conversation to have in the basement — not a promise that patching is always cheaper.

How to use the comparison

Open the boiler replacement bid calculator, enter the plant you are standing in, and put their patch number in “patch price they asked for.” The table scores that number against this visit, stacks this winter and the remaining seasons, and sets the total next to the plant bid. Nothing is uploaded.

This is the same arithmetic as how much to charge to replace a boiler. It is not a heat-loss calculation, a fuel-gas code determination, a chimney design, or a reason to refuse a customer — it is the walk-away number on the visit and the cash of one more winter.

Common questions

Should I patch a boiler for one more winter instead of replacing it?

Only after you price this visit and the extra no-heat calls the same plant will generate before spring. A $280 circulator special often sits under the walk-away on that visit even when three winters of patches still undercut a full replacement.

Does a $280 circulator swap cover a no-heat call?

Usually not. Loaded labor, the trip, and a $210 circulator stay on the ticket after you drop the Facebook number. On a typical 10-mile gas hot-water house the visit walk-away is still above $280.

When do patches cost more than replacing the boiler?

When a cracked section or a leaking heat exchanger comes back. Price this visit, the extra calls this winter, and the winters they want the old plant. A cheap circulator season can still undercut replacement; a section that needs $800 parts two more times this winter often does not.

should-i-take-a-saturday-boiler-call.htm.text:
← Boiler replacement bid calculator

Should I take a Saturday boiler call?

Owners call with a weekday number: “Can you come Saturday? The house is cold. Same $4,500?” That sounds like the same plant. It is not the same crew day. After-hours is time-and-a-half. A Friday-night no-heat call is not a stop you combine with a weekday route, so it is a second dispatch. Working in a house they stay in because the heat is out is the same wage on a slower hang.

Open the free boiler replacement bid calculator

Saturday is not the weekday bid

A weekday slot still carries the wage you already timed. After-hours raises that wage to time-and-a-half and adds a starting second trip. On a typical 80 MBH gas hot-water like-for-like — $48 wage, 32% burden, 15% overhead, 20% target margin, 10 miles — the weekday bid is $6,740.98. After-hours is $7,634.02. The walk-away jumps from $5,392.78 to $6,107.22. Taking $5,800 to “just do Saturday at a weekday-looking number” covers the weekday slot and loses $307.22 after hours. The Facebook $4,500 special loses even on Monday.

After-hours is $21,998.71 and the walk-away is $17,598.97. Taking $4,500 to “just swap it tonight” still loses money — even on the weekday.

This is not a patch visit or a customer-supplied crate

A $280 circulator patch is a service call, not a changeout — see should I patch this boiler for one more winter. Customer-supplied plants are their crate and a hang-only number — see should I install a customer-supplied boiler. After-hours is when you can stand in the basement. A toilet Saturday is an overflowing commode. A kitchen backsplash Saturday is tile overtime in a kitchen they still cook in. A walk-in shower Saturday is a wet-area crew. This prices a boiler replacement.

How to use the comparison

Open the boiler replacement bid calculator, pick the cheap-special or losing-job preset, and put their Saturday number in “price you’re considering.” The access table scores that number against a weekday slot, same-day with no heat, and after-hours / Saturday. Nothing is uploaded.

This is the same arithmetic as how much to charge to replace a boiler. It is not a labor-law determination, a union scale, or a reason to refuse a customer — it is the walk-away number on each access window.

Common questions

Should I take a Saturday or after-hours boiler replacement call?

Only after you price time-and-a-half plus a second emergency dispatch. A Friday-night no-heat call is not a stop you combine with a weekday route. A $4,500 Saturday special on an 80 MBH gas like-for-like sits under that walk-away number even on a weekday slot.

Does a same-day no-heat call change the bid?

Yes. Same wage, slower plant hang and punch-list. On a typical 80 MBH two-zone gas hot-water swap the same-day bid is $6,899.46 versus $6,740.98 when they can wait for a weekday slot.

Can I take the weekday $5,800 number on Saturday?

Usually not on the job they actually want. On a cheap gas like-for-like the after-hours walk-away is $6,107.22. $5,800 covers a weekday slot and loses $307.22 after hours. On a steam-to-hot-water conversion, $4,500 still loses money even on the weekday.

vs-a-flat-rate-boiler-special.html.text:
← Boiler Replacement Bid Calculator

This calculator vs. a flat-rate boiler special

"$4,500 boiler installed" is not a price for a boiler swap — it is a price for one specific MBH, fuel, and conversion type, quietly applied to every basement the truck pulls up to.

What a flat boiler special is

A flat special is the fastest way to quote: one headline number on a postcard or a website, read off and repeated. Homeowners shop it because it is easy to compare between bids, and it is the number a customer holding a competitor's flyer will ask you to match.

The number behind it was set for one job — one input MBH, one fuel, one conversion type (usually the simplest: hot-water like-for-like), one zone count, no liner, no tank change — and then reused for every boiler afterward, whether or not the next basement looks anything like the one the rate was built on.

What this calculator is

This page keeps no account and sends nothing to a server. You enter the input MBH, whether the job is hot-water or steam, like-for-like versus a condensing upgrade versus a steam-to-hot-water conversion, fuel, zone count, and extras such as a chimney liner or an indirect tank, plus your loaded labor and overhead. It prices the plant and the extra-work hours a conversion adds separately, and returns a walk-away price and an extra-work share below which the job loses money — for this basement, not a generic one.

What a flat special doesWhat this calculator does instead
Charges the same headline price whether the job is an 80 MBH gas hot-water like-for-like swap or a 140 MBH oil steam-to-hot-water conversion — a several-times difference in plant cost and labor for the same word "boiler". Prices the plant from the entered input MBH, fuel, and conversion type, so the two jobs above come out at different numbers instead of one.
Prices "a boiler" as one swap, with no separate line for venting changes, a condensate path, or the piping conversion a steam-to-hot-water job drags in. Times venting, condensate, and conversion labor as their own extra-work hours, so that work shows up instead of being absorbed into the plant price or skipped.
Assumes the existing chimney and hot-water setup carry over, so a job needing a new liner or an indirect tank gets quoted the same as one that does not. Adds a chimney-liner and indirect-tank line only when that scope is turned on, so the two jobs price differently.
Bakes payroll burden into a round "labor rate" nobody re-derives, so the rate quietly drifts from the crew's real loaded cost. Loads the entered hourly wage by the entered payroll-burden percentage every time, so labor cost tracks the actual burden rather than a memorized rate.
Gives the tech a price to quote, not a number to check a quote against when an owner asks to match a cheaper number. Reports the walk-away price and the extra-work share of the job, so a shopped price can be scored against real cost before the tech commits to it.

A flat special is not wrong because it is simple — it is wrong when it is applied outside the one job it was built for, and nothing about a postcard rate tells you when that has happened. This calculator does not replace judgment about your market; it replaces the arithmetic a flat rate skips.

Common questions

Why does a flat boiler special get the price wrong?

Because the plant and labor scale with MBH input, fuel, and conversion type, not with the word "boiler" alone. An 80 MBH gas hot-water like-for-like swap on two zones is a different job from a 140 MBH oil steam-to-hot-water conversion on four zones with an indirect tank and a chimney liner. A flat special quotes both the same and is wrong on one of them every time.

What does a flat special usually leave out entirely?

The extra work a steam-to-hot-water conversion drags in on top of the plant swap: venting changes, a condensate path if the new plant needs one, and the piping conversion itself. A rate built around "install a boiler" has nowhere to put those hours, so a tech pricing off the special alone is short before the truck is loaded.

What happens when the chimney or the tank has to change too?

A flat installed rate assumes the existing venting and hot-water setup carry over. A masonry chimney that needs a liner for a new appliance, or a plan that adds an indirect tank, is its own line of material and labor that a rate never asked about charges the same price for a job that takes longer and costs more.

Is a flat rate ever the right way to quote a boiler swap?

For a narrow band of near-identical jobs — same fuel, same conversion type, same zone count, no liner, no tank change — a flat rate can land close. The risk is applying it outside that band without noticing, because the postcard rate does not know which band a given basement is in and neither does the tech until the walkthrough.

Does this calculator know what to charge in my market?

No. It has no data on local rates, equipment cost, or what competitors charge. It takes the MBH, scope, fuel, zones, and your loaded labor and overhead, and turns them into a walk-away price and extra-work share for the job you describe — the arithmetic a flat rate skips, not a market survey.

Nothing here says or implies that quoting a flat boiler special is a bad-faith practice — it is a common, honest shortcut that works until the job stops matching the one the rate was set on. This page describes where that shortcut breaks down, not a fault in anyone who uses it.

Open the Boiler Replacement Bid Calculator and price your own job.
